summary: The kernel's pools of pipes, ptys, sockets and processes, filled at once, and made and closed a thousand times each without a leak of the heap; the program is tests/poolprobe.c

cases.behavior: Eight children at once each hold six pipes, then five pty masters, then six datagram sockets, then four children of their own, so that 48 pipes, 40 ptys, 48 sockets and 40 processes besides the probe are live together, and every holder exits 0

execution.cleanup: the holders and their children, each reaped on a pass; after a failed round the holders read the end of input on the word pipe and exit

assertions.checks: eight holders each open six pipes and report them, and each exits 0 after the word
eight holders each open five pty masters and report them, and each exits 0 after the word
eight holders each open six datagram sockets and report them, and each exits 0 after the word
eight holders each fork four children that wait for the word, report them, reap them and exit 0

cases.behavior: A thousand pipes, a thousand pty masters and a thousand datagram sockets, each made and closed in turn, leave the kernel heap's HeapUsed where it was and HeapPages within two pages of it, in one of three tries of each kind, since the process that reads the output can hold a block of the heap at one reading and not at the other

execution.cleanup: nothing to remove; each object is closed before the next is made

assertions.checks: a thousand pipes made and closed leave HeapUsed unchanged and HeapPages within two pages, in one of three tries
a thousand pty masters opened and closed leave HeapUsed unchanged and HeapPages within two pages, in one of three tries
a thousand datagram sockets made and closed leave HeapUsed unchanged and HeapPages within two pages, in one of three tries

native.reason: HeapUsed and HeapPages are the whole kernel's heap, which the services of a machine that is already up move while the thousands are made
